scenes.big: Splash in the eye? Don't rub!
scenes.en: Do this in the first minute.
scenes.say: Something splashed in your eye? Don't rub it! Here's what to do in the first minute.

scenes.en: Chemicals keep hurting the clear front of the eye. Water dilutes and washes them out.
scenes.say: Chemicals like floor cleaner or lime keep damaging the clear front window of the eye for as long as they stay. Water dilutes them and washes them away.

scenes.en: Clean running water for at least 15 minutes. Hold the eyelids open.
scenes.say: Do: rinse the eye right away with clean running water, for at least fifteen minutes. Hold the eyelids open. Take out contact lenses if you can.

scenes.en: Don't rub. No oil, milk, home remedies or drops unless a doctor says so.
scenes.say: Don't rub. Don't put in oil, milk, or any home remedy. And don't use any drops unless a doctor says so.

scenes.en: Don't press. Don't pull out anything stuck. Cover gently with a paper cup.
scenes.say: If something hit the eye, or is stuck in it, don't press, and don't pull it out. Cover the eye gently with a paper cup and go.

scenes.en: About half of eye injuries happen at home. Most can be prevented.
scenes.say: Did you know? Studies show about half of all eye injuries happen at home, and most can be prevented with simple protective glasses.

scenes.en: After rinsing, go straight to an eye hospital. Take the chemical bottle.
scenes.ta: கழுவிய பின் உடனே கண் மருத்துவமனைக்கு செல்லுங்கள்!
scenes.say: After rinsing, go straight to an eye hospital or emergency, even if it feels better. Take the chemical bottle with you.

scenes.en: Cleaners out of kids' reach. Goggles for strong chemicals. Regular eye tests.
scenes.say: Keep cleaners out of children's reach, wear goggles for strong chemicals, and book a regular eye test for the family.
